doc.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025

title: Visualizing the harmonica as a piano keyboard
summary: He explains he sees the harmonica as a piano keyboard, which led to simultaneous piano and harmonica playing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well said. The piano and harmonica in my mind are very different for at least one reason, when you’re playing the piano you can see the notes you’re playing.
When you’re playing the harmonica, do you always know what notes you’re playing?

Yes. I visualize the harmonica as a piano keyboard. Since the harmonica is totally invisible when you play it – I mean you pick it up, you look at it, and it’s got a bunch of these little holes – the holes don’t tell you much. And as soon as you put it in your mouth it’s gone anyway. So when I first started playing, when I was 18, and I was playing in that Northwestern jazz band and learning what thirteenth chords were and everything like that, which I didn’t know before, it was like what the hell is this? And reading all these Thad Jones arrangements and, you know, all that kind of stuff, and Brookmeyer charts and all these things that were like oooo what is this? That was when I was just starting to play the harmonica and playing my first blues licks. And then I wanted the harmonica to come up to the level of what I was doing on piano. So I’m, you know I’m playing with my eyes closed and like “What am I seeing, what am I seeing?” And after a while I realized I was seeing the piano keyboard as well as shapes and colors. So kind of all of the above. But it got to be more and more like a piano, which is how I eventually ended up playing a lot of simultaneous piano and harmonica. Because it’s one instrument.
I just realized something. You just answered my question by saying that. Because I saw some of your videos where you were playing unison piano and harmonica lines.
So you obviously know – you know that question was sort of I guess I’m thinking when you really are wailing on the harmonica, I was thinking to myself, “Does he know all the pitches actually?”
